title: Consolidate tool surface: 12 tools down to 8
description:
Remove 5 tools by absorbing their functionality into existing tools:

REMOVE:
- reinforce_learning → update_learning gains 'reinforce: true' flag (increments confidence, appends note)
- deprecate_learning → update_learning gains 'active: false' + 'deprecated_reason' field
- reactivate_learning → update_learning gains 'active: true' (clears deprecated_reason)
- learnings_for_area → filter_learnings (new tool) with codebase_areas param
- unlink_learnings → drop entirely (rarely used, usability trap requiring link UUID)

MODIFY:
- update_learning: add 'active' boolean param, 'deprecated_reason' string param, 'reinforce' boolean param
- When reinforce=true: increment confidence by 1, append note to rationale (same behavior as current reinforce_learning)
- When active=false: require deprecated_reason (same behavior as current deprecate_learning)
- When active=true on a deprecated learning: clear deprecated_reason (same as current reactivate_learning)

Final tool surface (8 tools): capture_learning, query_learnings, filter_learnings, get_learning, update_learning, review_learnings, link_learnings, get_linked
close_reason: Done. 12 tools consolidated to 7. reinforce/deprecate/reactivate absorbed into update_learning. learnings_for_area removed (filter_learnings will replace). unlink_learnings dropped. Build passes clean.

title: Make review_learnings accept project/area/date filters
description: review_learnings currently takes no parameters — always returns global stats. Add optional project, codebase_area, and date_range filters so you can get scoped views like 'stats for alludium this month'.

title: Expand source_type enum to support universal capture
description: Add new source_type values: note, idea, meeting_note, todo, reference. This enables Agent Cortex to replace Open Brain as a universal capture tool, not just code learnings. Requires DB enum change and type update in src/types/index.ts.
close_reason: Done. Added 5 new source_types: idea, note, preference, reference, troubleshooting. Updated TypeScript type, Zod enum, extraction.ts valid list, and AI prompt with descriptions for each new type. No DB migration needed.

comments.author: Donal
comments.text:
## Research: Source Type Expansion Plan

### How others categorize:
- **Mem0 OpenMemory**: user_preferences, implementation, troubleshooting, component_context, project_overview, incident_rca
- **Memori**: fact, preference, skill, context, rule (5 categories — clean and simple)
- **OMEGA**: No fixed enum — uses semantic search + auto-tagging instead of categories
- **Mem0 default catalog**: 15 categories (personal_details, family, sports, travel...) — too broad, not relevant for dev use

### Recommendation: Keep fixed enum, expand thoughtfully
Free-form strings sound flexible but kill filterability. Fixed enum + tags gives structure where it matters and flexibility via tags for everything else.

### Proposed new source_types (6 existing + 5 new = 11 total):
**Existing (keep):**
- pr_review, code_review, debugging, convention, architecture_decision, observation

**Add:**
- `idea` — fleeting ideas, possibilities, things to explore later
- `note` — general notes, context, meeting summaries, anything that doesn't fit elsewhere  
- `preference` — personal/team preferences for tools, patterns, workflows (maps to Mem0's user_preferences and Memori's 'preference')
- `reference` — links, docs, resources, external knowledge worth saving
- `troubleshooting` — solutions to specific problems, workarounds, gotchas (distinct from 'debugging' which is about the process — this is the answer)

### Why NOT more:
- 'todo' — that's what beads is for, don't duplicate
- 'meeting_note' — just use 'note' with a tag
- 'skill' — not relevant for this use case
- 'rule' — 'convention' already covers this

### Implementation:
1. Update Zod enum in src/index.ts
2. Update TypeScript union in src/types/index.ts  
3. Update extraction.ts prompt to include new types with descriptions so AI can auto-detect
4. DB: No CHECK constraint exists — validation is app-level only, so no migration needed
5. Default remains 'observation' (most generic)

title: Add time-range filters to query_learnings and learnings_for_area
description: Can't currently ask 'what did I learn this week?' or 'show learnings from last sprint'. Add from_date/to_date parameters to both query_learnings and learnings_for_area.
close_reason: Subsumed by filter_learnings (cortex-ggl) which includes from_date/to_date parameters

title: update_learning: add array parameter support to match capture_learning
description: capture_learning and update_learning have inconsistent parameter handling. capture_learning accepts arrays for metadata fields, but update_learning does not. This means you cannot correct metadata on an existing learning without deleting and recreating it — a poor UX. The fix is to make update_learning accept the same array formats that capture_learning does.
close_reason: Fixed: added coercedStringArray helper to index.ts — both capture_learning and update_learning now accept string[] or comma-separated string for codebase_areas and tags

title: Add duplicate detection on capture
description: Before inserting a new learning, run a cosine similarity check (threshold ~0.05). If a near-duplicate exists, warn or offer to merge/reinforce instead of creating a duplicate. Important as the corpus grows.
close_reason: Done. 2-layer dedup: exact text match (fast path) + cosine similarity >= 0.85 (semantic). Returns warning with existing learning details, does not block. force=true parameter to skip check. Scoped to same project + global.

comments.author: Donal
comments.text:
## Research: Duplicate Detection Implementation Plan

### Industry benchmarks:
- **OMEGA**: 3-layer dedup — SHA256 exact hash, cosine similarity >= 0.85 (blocks), Jaccard per-type. 55-95% similar content gets auto-evolved (merged) rather than blocked.
- **Mem0**: LLM inference pipeline for auto-dedup. Graph node matching threshold default 0.7 cosine, configurable 0.6-0.99.
- **Signals/Envisioning**: 3-stage — Jaccard title >0.8, category+semantic >0.75, pure semantic >0.8

### Recommended approach for Agent Cortex:
1. **Fast path**: Exact text match on `pattern` field (cheap, catches copy-paste dupes)
2. **Semantic check**: Cosine similarity >= 0.85 against existing active learnings in same project + global
3. **Behavior**: WARN, don't block. Return the existing learning with a message like 'Similar learning found (92% match). Consider reinforcing existing learning {id} instead.' Let the user decide.
4. **Project scoping**: Include project filter in dedup check — same pattern in different projects is legitimate

### Why 0.85 threshold:
- OMEGA uses 0.85 for semantic dedup (battle-tested, #1 on LongMemEval)
- Mem0 uses 0.7 for graph nodes but that's for entity merging (looser use case)
- 0.85 catches 'same idea, different phrasing' while avoiding false positives on merely related content
- The user said low-friction is priority — overzealous dedup is worse than occasional duplicates

### Implementation:
- Add dedup check in capture_learning handler AFTER embedding generation, BEFORE insert
- Query: `SELECT id, pattern, 1-(embedding <=> ::vector) AS sim FROM learnings WHERE active=true AND (project= OR project='global') ORDER BY embedding <=> ::vector LIMIT 3`
- If any result has sim >= 0.85, return warning with match details but still include the new learning's data
- Add optional `force: boolean` parameter to skip dedup check entirely

### Cost: One additional vector query per capture — negligible on hundreds/thousands of rows with HNSW index

title: Add hybrid search: full-text keyword search alongside semantic
description: Pure vector search misses exact keyword matches for technical terms (e.g. searching 'tRPC' semantically might miss exact hits). Add PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector/tsquery or pg_trgm) alongside existing pgvector cosine similarity. query_learnings should run both and merge/rank results. This is the single highest-impact improvement to retrieval quality.
close_reason: Implemented. Added tsvector generated column (pattern=A, rationale=B weights) + GIN index. hybridSearch() uses RRF (k=60, keyword=1.5x, semantic=1.0x) via CTEs with FULL OUTER JOIN. query_learnings now passes both query text and embedding. Build passes clean.

comments.author: Donal
comments.text:
## Research: Hybrid Search Implementation Plan

### Approach: PostgreSQL tsvector + pgvector with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)

**Why this approach:** Pure vector search got ~62% retrieval precision in benchmarks. Adding FTS + RRF bumped it to ~84%, with near-perfect exact-match queries. Zero additional infrastructure — all PostgreSQL.

### Schema changes:
- Add generated column: `search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', coalesce(pattern, '') || ' ' || coalesce(rationale, ''))) STORED`
- Add GIN index: `CREATE INDEX idx_learnings_fts ON learnings USING GIN (search_vector)`
- No new tables needed

### Search implementation (single SQL query using CTEs):
1. **CTE 1 (semantic)**: Existing pgvector cosine similarity query, returns top 20 with rank
2. **CTE 2 (keyword)**: FTS query using `websearch_to_tsquery` against search_vector, ranked by `ts_rank_cd`, returns top 20
3. **CTE 3 (fused)**: FULL OUTER JOIN on id, compute RRF score: `(1/(60+semantic_rank) * semantic_weight) + (1/(60+keyword_rank) * keyword_weight)`
4. ORDER BY hybrid_score DESC, LIMIT

### Key decisions:
- Use `websearch_to_tsquery` (not `plainto_tsquery`) — handles quoted phrases, OR, negation naturally
- Use `ts_rank_cd` (cover density ranking) over `ts_rank` — more intuitive for short text
- RRF k=60 (industry standard, tested across multiple benchmarks)
- Default weights: keyword=1.5, semantic=1.0 (technical content benefits from keyword bias per ParadeDB and Supabase guides)
- Consider pg_trgm as fallback for zero FTS results (catches typos like 'postgrsql')

### query_learnings changes:
- No new parameter needed — always run hybrid by default
- Optionally add `search_mode: 'semantic' | 'keyword' | 'hybrid'` parameter (default 'hybrid') for power users
- Existing similarity score replaced by hybrid_score (normalized 0-1)

### Reference implementations:
- dev.to/lpossamai hybrid search article (Node.js + PostgreSQL, exact same stack)
- Supabase hybrid search guide (uses same HNSW + GIN pattern)
- OMEGA uses same 5-stage pipeline (vector → FTS5 → type-weighted → re-rank → dedup)

title: Add filter_learnings tool with tag/source_type/date filters
description: query_learnings is semantic-only. learnings_for_area is area-only. Need a filter_learnings tool that accepts: tags[], source_type, date range (from/to), min_confidence, project. Enables queries like 'show all ideas tagged agent-swarm from last week'.
close_reason: Done. New filter_learnings tool with dynamic WHERE clause: tags, source_type, project, codebase_areas, from_date, to_date, min_confidence, include_deprecated. All existing GIN/B-tree indexes cover these columns. Also serves as the list/browse tool (call with no filters to see recent learnings). 8 tools total now.

comments.author: Donal
comments.text:
## Research: filter_learnings Tool Plan

### What it needs to do:
Structured parameter-based filtering (not semantic search). query_learnings is for 'find things like X'. filter_learnings is for 'show me all observations tagged agent-swarm from last week'.

### Parameters:
- `tags: string[]` — filter by tags (array overlap: ANY tag matches)
- `source_type: string` — filter by source_type enum value
- `project: string` — filter by project (includes 'global' by default)
- `codebase_areas: string[]` — filter by area (array overlap)
- `from_date: string` (ISO date) — created_at >= from_date
- `to_date: string` (ISO date) — created_at <= to_date
- `min_confidence: number` — confidence >= threshold
- `include_deprecated: boolean` (default false)
- `limit: number` (default 20, max 100)

### SQL approach:
Dynamic WHERE clause building — only apply filters for provided parameters. All existing GIN/B-tree indexes already cover these columns (tags, codebase_areas, source_type, project, active, confidence).

### Note on overlap with other beads:
- cortex-8s3 (time-range filters) is subsumed by this — from_date/to_date are part of filter_learnings
- cortex-2nn (scoped review_learnings) is partially subsumed — but review_learnings returns stats/aggregates, not individual learnings
- cortex-uya (min_similarity) applies to semantic search only, not this tool

### Recommendation: 
Implement cortex-ggl first, then close cortex-8s3 as 'covered by filter_learnings'. This avoids duplicating time-range filter logic across two tools.

title: Add batch_capture_learnings tool
description: learn-from-pr calls capture_learning N times serially. A batch_capture_learnings tool accepting an array of learnings would be more efficient and atomic for bulk ingestion workflows like PR review extraction.
close_reason: No real use case - a loop covers this, over-engineering

title: Add append_learning tool for incremental note building
description: Port Open Brain's append_thought concept. Allow appending text to an existing learning's pattern field (with separator). Re-generates embedding and metadata after append. Useful for building up notes over time.
close_reason: Redundant with update_learning - same effect, unnecessary complexity

title: Clean reinforcement history out of rationale field
description: reinforce_learning currently concatenates [Reinforced] notes into the rationale field, polluting it. Move to a separate reinforcement_history JSONB column or use the examples JSONB. Keeps rationale clean while preserving the audit trail.

title: Add min_similarity threshold to query_learnings
description: Currently query_learnings returns results regardless of relevance score. Add a min_similarity parameter (default 0.6) to filter out low-relevance noise from semantic search results.
